content.comment_body: Hello all, I need to control a device using a PLC. The device requires an SPDT switch to set its limits—the default state connects Set terminals to GND, and to change the setting, one is raised to +24V while the other remains at GND. Is there a method for using the PLC's output terminals to set these limits? I've attached a basic diagram to illustrate the wiring. Thanks.

If your [product_name] has relay outputs, these provide only make contacts (normally open) and not changeover contacts. To achieve changeover functionality, use the [product_name] outputs to drive external relays that offer changeover contacts.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to use PLC output terminals to simulate an SPDT switch for a device. It was clarified that the relay outputs on their [product_name] only offer make contacts (normally open), not changeover types. To achieve SPDT switching behavior, additional relays with changeover contacts must be integrated with the PLC outputs.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects PLC output terminals to directly replicate the actions of an SPDT (changeover) switch for controlling device limits.
